requirements.requirement: On node1, limit datauser to 100 MB under /srv/data using filesystem-level enforcement.
requirements.summary: A dedicated ext4 filesystem is mounted at /srv/data with user quotas active, and datauser has matching 102,400 KiB soft and hard limits. A 99 MiB write succeeded, while extending it beyond the quota failed with “Disk quota exceeded.” After restart, the mount, quota limits, account, permissions, sentinel data, and enforcement all recovered.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct tests demonstrate filesystem-enforced quota behavior before and after restart. The provider restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed outage, changed boot identity, and recovered filesystem, quota, account, permissions, and data. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing actions had a clear role: installing quota tooling and the missing kernel quota module, creating the account and dedicated filesystem, configuring the persistent mount and quota, performing bounded enforcement/recovery tests, cleaning test files, and executing the mandatory restart. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The initial unprivileged package-install attempt failed without evidence of mutation. Final observations show clean package state, no failed services, no listening sockets, and no abandoned test files.
